- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.67) and forecast spikes, reduce overshoot by 30-50% to avoid overreacting to sentiment-driven hype.
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.33) and forecast is low, avoid underestimating true volatility — add 15-25% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven downside risk.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days trending down), model should not over-forecast upward — cap forecast at 1.5x recent average.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment or price, model should not immediately follow with a 2x+ forecast — apply a 10-15 day lag correction to avoid momentum overfitting.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is erratic, use 3-day moving average of history to anchor forecast, avoiding sentiment-driven outliers.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >20% and sentiment is positive, assume sentiment is overvaluing — reduce forecast by 15-20% for next period.
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome by >15% over 3+ periods, check for sentiment lag — model may be underreacting to sentiment shifts; adjust by adding 10% to forecast for next period.
